messages:
Alex: Morning sync - want to capture a compact rollback/playbook approach for hosted, dedicated, private parity. Keep it operationally light.
Maya: We should be explicit about what "parity" means: identical API surface vs identical failure semantics. I vote for failure semantics parity.
Jorge: Agreed. Identical API surface is impossible across private installs. Failure semantics (observable + rollback behavior) is tractable.
Priya: Implementation constraints: private installs may have no direct control-plane access, slower network, and different evict semantics. That affects rollback latency.
Alex: Proposed separation: (A) Decision layer (global policy + triggers), (B) Execution layer (control-plane or local-agent), (C) Routing layer (sticky vs ephemeral).
Maya: For Execution layer, suggest three modes: centralized apply (hosted), delegated apply (dedicated relay), and local-agent apply (private). Each must support the same idempotent rollforward/rollback ops.
Jorge: How about a small state-machine encoded in manifests: desired_state {version:v2, rollback_point:v1, roll_policy:manual|auto}, and agents act on it. Agents must ack operations with a signed event.
Priya: Local-agent can sign ack with installer key so control-plane trusts it. For privacy we can store only hashes + high level metrics to avoid payload leakage.
Alex: Routing notes: use tenant-level affinity token with TTL. On rollouts, new variant gets new token; on rollback set TTL=0 so new requests favor old variant. Existing pinned sessions continue.
Maya: Need to handle long-running streaming sessions. We should drain new-stream acceptances for N seconds, not immediately cut. Add a heuristics value per-deployment.
Jorge: Observability triggers: token-error-rate, token-tail-latency, and eval-quality-delta. Variant of these for private where eval-quality-delta comes from local-agent.
Alex: Auto-rollback policy draft: if token-error-rate > 3x baseline for 3m OR P99 > +250ms for 5m then trigger conditional rollback; require human approval if cross-plane change.
Priya: For schema-only changes we can attempt an auto-shim that translates old manifest keys; if shim fails, reject at manifest apply time. That avoids global rollbacks.
Maya: Playbook items to add: cache invalidation TTL steps, KV-cache drain, routing-pin adjustment, audit event emit, paging thresholds, and a rollback postmortem checklist.
Jorge: Small decision table I sketched: 
```
change_class,trigger_auto,require_agent_ack,operator_restore_time
control-plane,yes,yes,~2m
runtime,conditional,yes,~5-20m
schema,no,yes,~10-60m
crossplane,manual,yes,~varies
```
Alex: Security: any rollback action must produce an auditable signed event and require RBAC scope. For Dedicated/Private the local-agent signing cert maps to customer tenancy.
Priya: SDK change: add header `X-RW-Rollback-Policy: default|opt_out|strict`. Document behavior: if opt_out, SDK pins to the variant and ignores auto rollback routing flips for that session.
Maya: Caveat: opt_out complicates bulk rollbacks. We should limit opt_out to dev keys or shorter TTLs and surface warnings in console.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging canary 3959991144 started for rollback flow validation.
Alex: Next actions: Maya write mini-RFC with decision matrix and playbook skeleton; Jorge build metric hooks; Priya sketch local-agent ack schema and SDK header patch. I'll bake a tiny audit-event spec. Revisit in 48h.
